clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old female with a history of AIH/PBC overlap syndrome and cirrhosis presented for re-evaluation of a hepatic nodule. An abdominal ultrasound in October 2020 identified a 9/10 mm subcapsular hypoechoic nodule in hepatic segment VI/VII. Blood analysis showed slightly increased AFP (10.8 ng/ml). By June 2021, a follow-up abdominal ultrasound revealed the nodule had grown to 29 mm. A liver MRI using gadoxetate disodium showed the nodule to be hypovascular and non-specific, classified as LI-RADS 3. Subsequently, a liver biopsy in July 2021 revealed moderately differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma (G2), pT2 Nx Mx L0 V1 R0, with specific immunohistochemistry findings (Hep Par-a positive, Glypican3 positive, CD34 positive). A resected lymph node showed no malignant cells, confirming N0 status. Post-surgical follow-up with a CT scan in January 2022 showed no sign of tumor recurrence.
